objective: Recognize SQL injection types -- in-band, blind (inferential) and out-of-band -- and the SQL injection methodology and evasion techniques
secondaryObjectives: Implement SQL injection countermeasures such as parameterized queries, input validation and least-privilege database accounts

Analyze web application threats with the web application hacking methodology: authentication, authorization, access control, sessions, input validation, logic flaws, and web APIs, webhooks and web shells

brief.situation: You are the application security engineer at Larkspur Travel, a fictional booking site. At 15:00 the web application firewall, in detect-only mode, flags requests to the destination search from 203.0.113.70, and the database's slow-query log is filling. Work out what kind of attack it is, stop it, fix it properly, find out what was read, and write it up.
handover: You own the booking application and can ship emergency changes, switch WAF rules and turn features off with flags. The app's database login is currently db_owner.
This is your own application: everything here is defensive work on systems you are responsible for.
howItWorks: Each task takes time: choose it, then let it finish, which moves the clock by the minutes it takes. The attacker keeps working on the same clock.
New alerts and log lines appear in the console as they happen.
When you close the incident you notify, record it and explain your reasoning.

source.note: Fifteen minutes until the attacker has mapped the tables is the author's figure.
Ten minutes for the attacker to vary encoding and addresses after being blocked is the author's figure.

read.label: Read the WAF detections, the slow-query log and the search handler

effects.log: You read the detections, the slow queries and the handler's code.

effects.finding: No errors and no data in the responses, but each true condition makes the query take 5 seconds: time-based blind (inferential) SQL injection, possible because the handler joins user text into the SQL.

effects.log: The address is blocked. Within a minute the same requests come from another address.

wafBlock.label: Switch the WAF's SQL injection rules for /search from detect to block

effects.log: Requests matching the signatures are blocked. Signatures match patterns; a determined attacker varies them.

filter.label: Add a filter that strips quotes and SQL keywords from the search box

effects.log: The filter is live. It breaks searches for destinations with apostrophes, and a blocklist can be encoded around.

flagOff.label: Turn the destination search off with its feature flag

effects.log: Search is off: customers browse by region instead. The injectable code no longer runs.

fix.label: Ship the fix: a parameterized query for the search handler (emergency change, 20 min)

effects.log: The handler now binds 'dest' as a parameter; no input can change the query's structure.

restore.label: Turn search back on with the fixed handler

effects.log: Search is back, running the parameterized query.

effects.log: app_search can now read only the search views; the customers table is out of its reach.

writeup.question: For the incident record: what kind of injection this was and how you knew, how you stopped it, and what makes it stay stopped.

parts.label: Type and stage
parts.criteria: Names time-based blind (inferential) injection from the evidence (no errors or data in responses, 5-second delays on true conditions) and places the attacker in the methodology (fingerprinting, then mapping tables, then extracting).
parts.modelAnswer: No errors or data came back, but true conditions took exactly 5 seconds: time-based blind injection. The attacker was fingerprinting and would move on to the table list and then customer rows.

parts.label: Containment against evasion
parts.criteria: Stops the vulnerable code from running (feature flag) rather than relying on an address block, WAF signatures or a keyword filter, which are evaded by changing addresses, case and encoding.
parts.modelAnswer: I turned search off: an address block, WAF signatures and a keyword filter are all evaded by rotating addresses and encoding.

parts.label: Lasting fix
parts.criteria: Fixes with a parameterized query, moves the database login to least privilege, restores the feature after the fix, and checks the audit log for what was read.
parts.modelAnswer: A parameterized query fixes the cause; a read-only login on the search views limits any future flaw; search came back after the fix; the audit log shows what was read.

expertPath.text: Read the evidence: no errors, 5-second delays on true conditions: time-based blind injection. Export the logs.
Turn search off with its flag; the vulnerable code stops running.
Ship the parameterized query, move the login to read-only views, turn search back on.
Check the audit log for what was read; tell the handler and the privacy officer; record it.

handled.headline: Good: recognized, stopped, fixed at the cause
handled.body: Blind injection leaves no errors, only timing. You stopped the code from running, then fixed the query and the login's privileges.

handledCostly.headline: Stopped, with gaps
handledCostly.body: The criteria show what cost you: the tables mapped first, no least privilege, no audit check, or search left off.

dumped.headline: The customers table was read
dumped.body: An address block is evaded in a minute. Stop the vulnerable code from running, then fix it.

leftOpen.headline: Still injectable
leftOpen.body: WAF signatures and keyword filters are evaded by encoding and case changes. Only the parameterized query closes it.

time_up.headline: Time up
time_up.body: No incident record was written before the run's hard limit.

scoring.modelReasoning: No errors or data in the responses, but true conditions take exactly 5 seconds: time-based blind (inferential) SQL injection, made possible by a handler that joins user text into SQL. Export the logs and turn the feature off so the vulnerable code stops running; an address block, WAF signatures and a keyword filter are evaded by rotating addresses and encoding. Ship a parameterized query, move the database login to least privilege, turn search back on, and check the audit log for what was read before telling the handler and the privacy officer.
